statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is a valid answer for rains when one exists, and r is the empty vector otherwise. A vector v of i64 is a valid answer for rains exactly when: (1) len(v) = n; (2) for every i with 0 <= i < n, if rains[i] > 0 then v[i] = -1, and if rains[i] = 0 then v[i] > 0; (3) the following simulation, run for i = 0,1,...,n-1 with an initially empty set F of lake numbers, never produces a flood: if rains[i] > 0, then a flood occurs if rains[i] is in F, otherwise rains[i] is added to F; if rains[i] = 0, then v[i] is removed from F if it is in F, otherwise F is unchanged. Thus, if at least one valid answer exists, the returned r must satisfy (1)-(3); if no valid answer exists, the returned r must have len(r) = 0. Every valid answer is accepted, including valid answers whose dry-day entries are arbitrary positive i64 lake numbers not occurring in rains.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) is either 0 or n. Equivalently, if r is nonempty, then len(r) = n.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) > 0, for every i with 0 <= i < n and rains[i] > 0, we have r[i] = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) > 0, for every i with 0 <= i < n and rains[i] = 0, we have r[i] > 0. The value r[i] may be any positive i64 lake number; it is not required to occur among the positive entries of rains.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) > 0, the drying schedule r is flood-free: let F be initially empty; for i = 0,1,...,n-1, if rains[i] > 0 then require rains[i] not in F and then add rains[i] to F; if rains[i] = 0 then remove r[i] from F if it is present, otherwise leave F unchanged. No rainy day may find its lake already in F.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 0 if and only if there does not exist any vector v with len(v) = n such that (i) for every i, v[i] = -1 when rains[i] > 0 and v[i] > 0 when rains[i] = 0, and (ii) the simulation with v described in spec_6 has no flood. Moreover, if len(r) > 0, then r itself satisfies (i) and (ii), i.e. r is a valid schedule.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r with len(r) = n, and r[i] = -1 for every 0 <= i < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000. Assume additionally that rains[i] > 0 for every 0 <= i < n, and that the positive values are pairwise distinct: for every 0 <= i < j < n, rains[i] != rains[j].

statement: The function returns the empty vector, i.e. len(r) = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000. Assume additionally that rains[i] > 0 for every 0 <= i < n, and that some lake rains twice: there exist i and j with 0 <= i < j < n and rains[i] = rains[j].

statement: The function returns a result r with len(r) = n and r[i] > 0 for every 0 <= i < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(rains). The slice is nonempty (n >= 1), and for every i with 0 <= i < n we have 0 <= rains[i] <= 1000000000. Assume additionally that rains[i] = 0 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) > 0, let i be any index with 0 <= i < n and rains[i] = 0, and let F_i be the set of full lakes immediately before day i in the simulation of r (F_0 is empty). If r[i] is not in F_i, then replacing the single entry r[i] by any positive i64 lake d yields another valid answer for rains: the modified vector has length n, has -1 exactly on rainy days, has a positive value on every dry day, and its simulation is flood-free.
